Column looks

Give a column a look and every cell in it is shown that way, in every row. To colour only some values, for example “Out of stock” in red, use Colour rules instead.

  • Session Ordinary Change
  • Seats left 1 240 A bar behind the number Change
  • Booking Book a seat A button, if the cell holds a link Change

  • 1 240 A bar behind the number. The bigger the number, the longer the bar, so rows can be compared at a glance. Cells without a number stay plain.
  • In stock Every value as a pill. Each value sits in a small rounded label, like a tag. Best for short words such as a status or a category.
  • 1 240 The whole column in a colour. Every cell in the column gets the colour you pick, so one column stands out, for example a total.
  • Open A button, if the cell holds a link. A cell holding a web address (https://…) becomes a button with the words you type in “Button text”. Cells without an address stay as they are.
  • If a colour rule also matches a cell, the rule’s colour wins for that cell. That way one row can still stand out in a column that has a look.
